1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Felsheim for three days. In the spring, Anna Weber's older sister had left for Berlin, and since then Anna had been running the village's little pharmacy on her own.
At nightfall she closed the shutters, counted the day's takings, blew out the lamp and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when someone began hammering at the door downstairs. A man's voice called out: "Is anyone there?"
A young man stood at the door, soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in a bloody cloth. He introduced himself as Konrad Wolf and said he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need a bandage," Wolf said quietly. "I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred marks be enough?"
He pulled a letter wrapped in oil paper from his jacket. "This letter has to be at Steinbach Monastery before the eighteenth of May."
Anna had been blind as a bat: only now did she notice how pale he was.
Even so, she did not take his money, and only said: "Tomorrow morning I'll take you into the mountains."
2: At daybreak they set off. Anna carried a basket on her back, with bread, healing herbs and an old umbrella inside.
Halfway up they met old Hans Becker, chopping wood. He set the axe aside and said quietly that the evening before, three strangers at the village entrance had asked after a wounded young man.
“Take the path, Anna,” Hans Becker said. “The road isn’t safe.” Anna thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Anna went first, setting each step carefully. Wolf followed her in silence.
Toward midday the rain stopped, the fog slowly lifted, and in the distance the roof of Steinbach Abbey appeared. At the gate stood a nun, Sister Hildegard, who welcomed guests at the abbey.
Sister Hildegard took the letter, examined the red seal and nodded. “The abbess has been waiting 2 years for this letter.”
Wolf said to Anna, “I owe you my life.” Anna smiled. “Then next time, repair the roof of my pharmacy.” Wolf stayed at the abbey.
In the evening Anna went down the mountain alone. When she got home it was already dark; she lit the lamp and sat for a long time behind the counter.
